scope: offline process-restart counterexample using exact retained receipt fixture; no GUI/model/input
H: The in-memory ReplanReceiptLedger will remint a token for the exact same authority_end_id after process restart because issued_ids is not persisted.
T: One first-outcome two-process test. Process A issues and consumes the exact retained receipt. Process B starts with a fresh empty ledger and replays the byte-identical receipt. No retries.
D: FAIL_CURRENT_CANDIDATE if process B successfully issues a fresh token for the same authority_end_id; PASS_CURRENT_CANDIDATE only if replay is rejected without extra external state.
C: A hidden persistent store or receipt mutation could explain rejection; both are excluded by using only the exact upstream Python files and fixture and a new Python interpreter.
U: This proves only process-memory restart replay, not machine reboot, filesystem durability, transport duplication, or live input consequences.
